## 問題

`main` でローカルの `make integrity` が fail していた: `redact_check.py` が `evidence/repository-snapshots/KSE2026/comments.json:94` に name-denylist hit（1 finding）を報告．KSE2026 self-snapshot の comment body に，`private/redact-names.txt` の denylist に載る個人名（host 識別ハンドル）が生のまま含まれていたため．

**CI の `integrity` job が main で green な理由**: denylist ファイルは private（untracked・gitignored）で CI 環境に存在せず，`redact_check.py` の name パターンがロードされない．つまり local-gate-only の failure だが，denylist を持つローカル環境では以後すべての PR の commit 前ゲートを塞いでいた．

## 変更

1. **`scripts/export_repo_snapshot.py`**: `scrub()` は email しかマスクしていなかった．`redact_check.py` の `load_name_denylist()` を鏡写しにした `load_name_patterns()` helper を追加し，`private/redact-names.txt` が存在する時のみ denylist 名を `<name-redacted>` にマスク（既存の `<email-redacted>` 書式に整合）．ファイル不在時は無効 — その環境では `redact_check.py` も同じ名前を検出できないため，gate と scrub は乖離せず同時に degrade する．さらに codex review の P1 指摘（`author_name`・milestone・label・tag 名などの未 scrub フィールド）を受け，`write_json()` 内で `scrub_tree()` により全 string 値へマスクを適用（b093f98）．変更は helper 中心の小さな塊にまとめ，#70 で予定される exporter 変更との rebase 衝突を最小化した．
2. **`evidence/repository-snapshots/KSE2026/`**: exporter 再実行（`gh api` 経由）で再収集（手編集なし）．issues 79 件・comments 126 件・commits 82 件，`head_sha_at_fetch=e65b872e…`，`fetched_at=2026-07-26T08:18:53Z`．scrub 産物のマスクは **comment body 1 箇所のみ**（当初この PR body と 0a271ca の commit message は「issue body 側の残存 1 件も追加でマスク（計 2 箇所）」と記載していたが，独立レビュー指摘により誤りと確認し訂正: issues.json 中の `<name-redacted>` 出現は issue #79 自身の本文がマスク書式を字義通り引用しているもので，live の issue body にも同一に存在し，denylist パターンは live body に hit しない．8cfaca3 で `provenance/ai-use.md` の該当行も訂正済み）．影響のない leray-hopf snapshot は再収集していない．
3. **`provenance/source-inventory.md`**: KSE2026 行を再収集後の件数・fetched_at・head sha に更新．mediation census 行に「census は自己記述された 2026-07-24 時点の snapshot（git 履歴から参照可能）を対象とし，本再収集後も再計算していない」と注記（census JSON は入力 snapshot の `head_sha_at_fetch`/`fetched_at` を自身の中に記録している）．
4. **`provenance/ai-use.md`**: 規則 6 の 1 行追記（レビュー指摘の訂正を含む）．

## Validation

- `python3 scripts/redact_check.py --dir evidence --dir claims --dir analysis --dir provenance --dir notes --dir paper` — 修正前: 77 files / **1 finding**（comments.json:94）．修正後: 77 files / **0 findings**（denylist 存在下）

- `make lint` — green（unittest 6 件 + prose scanner．chktex は本環境に不在で skip；CI が `REQUIRE_CHKTEX=1` で実測）
- `make selftest` — 73 passed / 0 failed（chktex 不在で 6 ブロック skip，AGENTS.md 記載どおり）
- `scrub_tree()` がコミット済み snapshot 全 12 ファイル（KSE2026 + leray-hopf）に対し no-op であることを機械確認（コミット済みデータ = 新コードの出力．fixup での再 export 不要）

## 備考

- snapshot の diff が大きいのは再収集が 2026-07-24 以降の repo 活動（issues 65→79，comments 72→126，commits 48→82）を取り込むため．point-in-time の旧 snapshot は git 履歴に残る．

## Motivation

Lean Eval is a submission-based benchmark and leaderboard for completing isolated Lean theorem holes. Its catalogue already includes substantial statements from analysis and PDE, including the Cauchy–Kovalevskaya theorem, Sobolev embedding in the Morrey regime, and radial symmetry for semilinear Poisson equations.

This is relevant prior work, but its evaluation unit differs materially from this paper. Lean Eval fixes a theorem statement, dependencies, and trusted scaffolding, then evaluates whether a solver can produce an accepted proof term. Our project instead studies persistent repository-level formalisation: mathematical decomposition, library and API development, multi-agent coordination, integration across PRs, review, literature alignment, and axiom management over an extended campaign.

## Requested revision

Add a brief mention in the Introduction or Related Work. Detailed discussion is unnecessary, but the paper should explicitly distinguish:

- isolated theorem-completion benchmarks;
- end-to-end, repository-level formalisation campaigns;
- proof generation as one component of a broader orchestration and verification workflow.

Possible wording:

> Recent systems have demonstrated strong performance on isolated theorem-completion benchmarks such as Lean Eval, including benchmark statements encoding major results from analysis and partial differential equations. Our work addresses a different scale of formalisation: a persistent repository-level campaign requiring mathematical decomposition, library development, integration, review, and axiom management in addition to theorem proving.

## Cautions

- Do not describe every Lean Eval entry as a complete reusable formalisation of the named theorem.
- Prefer wording such as “benchmark statement”, “theorem-completion problem”, or “accepted proof submission”.
- Cite the Lean Eval website and, where appropriate, its repository or benchmark description.
- Keep the comparison concise; its purpose is positioning, not a detailed audit of individual submissions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Lean Eval is cited in the Introduction or Related Work.
- The manuscript clearly states the difference in task granularity and workflow scope.
- No unsupported claim is made that Lean Eval entries constitute full from-first-principles formal developments.
title: Position the work against Lean Eval theorem-completion benchmarks

## Purpose

If the requested ChatGPT data export arrives before the manuscript/provenance freeze, inspect it to determine whether the author-facing ChatGPT conversations can be joined to GitHub Connector writes and thereby strengthen issue #60's provenance account.

This is a **time-bounded optional follow-up**. Absence, delay, or insufficient structure in the export must not block the paper.

Related: #60, #66, PR #68.

## Security and data-handling constraints

- Treat the complete export ZIP and all raw conversation data as private source material.
- Do **not** commit the ZIP, raw conversations, account metadata, unrelated chats, prompts, hidden tool payloads, personal data, tokens, or email addresses.
- Work only in a gitignored private workspace until redaction is complete.
- Any committed derivative must pass the repository leakage and redaction gates and contain only the minimum fields needed for auditability.
- Do not upload the unredacted export to a third-party service or model.

## Questions

1. What files and schemas does the export contain?
   - conversation IDs, titles, timestamps and message trees;
   - visible user/assistant messages;
   - tool-call or connector metadata, arguments, responses, artifact IDs or URLs, if present;
   - edited/deleted message history, if any.
2. Can individual ChatGPT interactions be joined to GitHub artifacts using:
   - exact comment/review/issue IDs;
   - exact URLs;
   - normalized body hashes;
   - repository + issue/PR number + timestamp windows;
   - weaker sequence-based reconstruction only where exact keys are unavailable?
3. What fraction of the `t-uda` posts attributed to `chatgpt-codex-connector` can be linked to an explicit preceding owner instruction?
4. Does the export materially change any current claim in the role model, intervention traces, mediation census, or manuscript?

## Method

1. Inventory the export without assuming that tool calls are present.
2. Define a small local parser using the Python standard library only.
3. Extract only candidate conversations relevant to `uda-lab/leray-hopf`, `uda-lab/leray-hopf-notes`, and `uda-lab/KSE2026`.
4. Join against the frozen GitHub snapshots using a confidence hierarchy:
   - `exact-id` — artifact ID or canonical URL present on both sides;
   - `exact-body` — normalized body hash plus repository/artifact identity;
   - `time-and-context` — unique match by repository, issue/PR number, action type and narrow timestamp window;
   - `reconstructed` — sequence/context inference, explicitly labelled and never counted as exact.
5. Report coverage separately for issue/PR creation, issue comments, formal PR reviews, and other write actions.
6. Record unmatched and ambiguous cases; do not force a match.

## Candidate committed derivatives

Only if the export supports useful reconstruction:

- a schema and limitations note under `analysis/`;
- a redacted linkage summary under `evidence/metrics/` containing no conversation text beyond short, necessary excerpts;
- a reproducible parser that accepts a local path but does not bundle raw data;
- narrow corrections to #60/#66 artifacts where the new evidence changes confidence or attribution.

Suggested linkage fields:

```text
conversation_id_hash
message_timestamp
repository
artifact_kind
artifact_number
artifact_id
join_method
confidence
authorization_present
notes
```

Hash or pseudonymize conversation identifiers unless an unhashed identifier is demonstrably necessary.

## Non-goals

- Publishing or archiving the full ChatGPT export.
- Treating a connector tool call as proof that the human read every final byte before transmission.
- Inferring productivity or causal effectiveness from message counts.
- Reopening settled owner authority: a write issued from the authenticated `t-uda` account remains owner-authorized under the recorded owner policy.
- Broad manuscript rewriting. Any manuscript change requires separate owner review and must preserve PR #59's editorial discipline.

## Stop conditions

Close as `not planned` with a short limitations note if any of the following holds:

- the export arrives after the relevant freeze;
- conversation/tool metadata is absent and visible text does not support reliable joins;
- safe redaction would remove the information needed for useful reconstruction;
- the result would add volume without changing confidence, attribution, or a publication claim.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Raw export remains untracked and private.
- [ ] Export schema and data availability are documented precisely.
- [ ] Join hierarchy and ambiguity policy are defined before matching.
- [ ] Coverage counts distinguish exact, reconstructed, ambiguous and unmatched records.
- [ ] Every committed derivative passes `make integrity`, `make lint`, and relevant self-tests.
- [ ] Existing provenance claims are changed only where the export supplies stronger evidence.
- [ ] The final issue/PR report states whether the export materially improved the paper's provenance account.
title: Time-bounded follow-up: reconstruct Connector provenance from ChatGPT data export

Closes #66
Refs #60

Wave A (#64, `fe8fbeb`) delivered the evidence layer. This is the analysis layer:
a role/authority model with a full passage audit, a set of intervention traces
covering both effective mediation and drift, and the publication-metadata
mechanism.

## What changed

| File | |
|---|---|
| `analysis/author-interface-model.md` | new — actor model + 282-row audit ledger + the three open items |
| `analysis/author-interface-traces.md` | new — 11 traces, drift included, excluded-with-reasons, incident and log-gap mapping |
| `notes/deanonymization-checklist.md` | new — 26 identity leaks + the artifact-availability option matrix |
| `paper/main.tex` | `\ifanonymous` switch + `\IEEEoverridecommandlockouts` + the funding `\thanks` |
| `provenance/ai-use.md` | AI-use record updated for the takeover (AGENTS.md rule 6) |

## B1 — role and authority model

The governing premise (owner, 2026-07-25: decisions issued from the `t-uda`
account are owner authority regardless of who drafted the wording) was **applied,
not relitigated**. `scientific owner` is untouched everywhere. Of **282** ledger
rows, **276 are "no change"** — 1 change-required, 3 owner-decision, 2 referred to
B3. (The first draft said 168; both reviewers counted independently and caught it.)

**Every line number was re-derived against `fe8fbeb`.** That turned out to matter:

> **Two of the three items the issue lists as open no longer exist in the manuscript.**
> PR #59 (`fc912b9`) got there first.
>
> | Item | Then | Now on `fe8fbeb` |
> |---|---|---|
> | 1a | `03-agent-workflow.tex`: "until the supervisor caught the discrepancy" | **deleted** — `supervisor`/`caught` appear nowhere in that file |
> | 1b | `04-incidents.tex`: "an incidental owner status check" | **rewritten** — `04:107-108` now reads "An owner requested a status check when only 606\,MiB remained available." |
> | 2 | `05-discussion.tex`: "the scientific owner's **direct** supervision" | **rewritten, "direct" gone** — `05:60-61` now reads "The owner's supervision was part of the harness and cannot be separated from its outcome." |

Both were still investigated on the evidence, because the analysis-layer claims
survive and Wave C could reconsider restoring prose. Findings:

- **1a is *accurate*, and its removal was editorial, not evidential.** The raw
  transcript (session `7e6156bf`, EV-1669) shows the human typed two messages
  directly into the session at `2026-07-10T00:37:21.889Z` and `00:43:22.204Z`,
  independently observing that review had completed while merge was stalled and
  correctly hypothesizing a defective monitor. The detection channel was direct
  human keystrokes — **not** connector-mediated. Recommendation: do not restore
  the sentence (Section III no longer carries that narrative), but the analysis
  ledger's evidence cell can cite the two timestamps.
- **1b is correctly stated and deliberately weaker than the evidence allows.** At
  `2026-07-18T07:40:10.101Z` the owner's entire message was the single word
  `status`. The card, ranking, and session index all say the owner supplied a
  *trigger*, not a detection — which is exactly right. The old word "incidental"
  was also correct and more informative.
- **2: recommend no change.** The current sentence asserts *inseparability* and is
  silent on channel, so no mediation fact can falsify it. Adding "(tool-assisted)"
  would be the drift this work was told to avoid.

**One change is required, and it goes to Wave C, not here.** `INC-005`'s timeline
step 4 records the orchestrator's 06:28–06:31Z misdiagnosis but omits two owner
utterances from the same window. At `06:28:39.808Z` the owner asked for status —
so that check was **prompted, not autonomous**. At `06:30:55.545Z` the owner
identified the `.lake` cache-sharing deviation (trigger cause (b)) and, **in the
same message, explicitly declined to act on it**: 「まぁ良いですよ．時間はあるので．」
That is roughly 70 minutes before the OOM surfaced.

The first draft wrote this up as "a real human detection the card under-credits".
Both reviewers refuted that: the full quote does not support it. It is an
observation paired with a decision not to act, and it is part of why trigger cause
(b) persisted. The file now says so, and tells Wave C in writing not to record it
as human detection. The draft's further generalisation — that the corpus errs
toward under-crediting human acts — rested entirely on this one row and is
**withdrawn**.

## B2 — intervention traces

Eleven traces, each anchored to a `make verify`-resolvable identifier, every
reconstruction labelled with `evidence_type` + confidence, no productivity or
causal inference anywhere. **Drift was found** — five carry it: a six-issue connector batch
where the Lean-source pre-wash gate corrected **all six** (overstated open work, a
collision with in-flight work, a misquoted Lean signature); a connector-created PR
merged 5m15s after opening with `reviews = []` and `reviewRequests = []`; a review
point issued and then explicitly **retracted** — 7m25s later, before the
implementer responded, so a same-round self-correction and weaker evidence than
the first draft implied; a verdict resting on stale README content, reversed 28
minutes on; and recurring self-corrections against stale issue bodies.

T11 exists because a reviewer caught `leray-hopf#190` being excluded as a
"formulaic merge approval" when it in fact **withholds approval** over a
documentation overclaim — on the same manual-attestation-versus-CI distinction the
ledger leans on elsewhere. An exclusion whose stated reason is false has the same
effect as selective reporting, whichever way it happened.

The negative findings are stated too, so the drift set is not inflated: no
connector-created issue closed `not planned`, no connector-created PR closed
unmerged, and no mathematically wrong connector-issued claim found. The full
search scope (repos, endpoints, numbers, keyword sweep over all 442 leray-hopf
comments) is enumerated in the file, along with what could not be searched
(deleted/minimized comments, edit history, the ChatGPT side).

Two findings worth surfacing:

- **The interface is absent from INC-002 and INC-004** — the two incidents where
  pre-merge detection worked best. Its GitHub-side presence in INC-001 is total
  (`leray-hopf#145`, `#157`, `#158`, `#177`, `#178` are all connector-attributed);
  the Lean-side repair PRs are not.
- **The single self-describing record (`leray-hopf#177`) and the largest connector
  burst (11 issues in 15 seconds, `leray-hopf#146`–`#156`) both sit in uncovered
  session-log windows.** Everything reported about them is GitHub-side primary
  evidence with no session-log corroboration.

`leray-hopf#177`'s ruling is scoped to **review independence** (a ChatGPT post-hoc
audit is an interested-party review). It explicitly declines to dispute commit
attribution and says nothing about decision authority. The file keeps those apart.

## B3 — publication metadata

**The B3 premise in the issue was wrong and is corrected here.** `paper/main.tex:36`
has read `\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{Anonymous Author(s)}}` since PR #59, so
"default to the current non-anonymous output" cannot hold — today's output *is* the
anonymous one.

Design taken: **default `\anonymoustrue`**, which reproduces today's PDF exactly
rather than pre-empting the deferred decision. The acknowledgment sits in the
non-anonymous branch (the grant number is publicly searchable, so suppressing it
under anonymity is the correct behaviour). The flip is one line;
`% TODO(owner)` marks the real byline, which only the owner can supply.

Two things that are load-bearing and should not be "cleaned up":

- **`\IEEEoverridecommandlockouts` is required.** IEEEtran redefines `\thanks` in
  conference mode to *silently swallow its argument* — the acknowledgment would
  compile cleanly and print nothing. Confirmed in the class source and in the log.
- `\thanks` goes **inside** `\author{}`, where IEEEtran flushes it at `\maketitle`
  as an unmarked first-page footnote; a standalone `\footnote` would be numbered
  and land in body text. Trailing `%` on the conditional lines is required or
  ChkTeX Warning 1 fails `make lint`.

`notes/deanonymization-checklist.md` enumerates 26 leaks with `file:line`, marking
which the switch handles (2) and which need separate work (the rest), plus what was
checked and found absent (no email, no session UUID, no affiliation block, empty
PDF `/Author` and `/Title`, no image EXIF surface).

## For the owner to decide — nothing below was decided here

1. **Artifact availability.** `05-discussion.tex:67-69` tells readers that evidence
   excerpts, manifests, and scripts "are available in the paper repository", but
   `uda-lab/KSE2026` is private, is **never named in the paper**, and has no bib
   entry, URL, or DOI. Two independent failures stack: the referent cannot be
   identified, and guessing it returns 404. A reader can reach `uda-lab/leray-hopf`,
   which supports CLM-001 but none of CLM-002/003/004 — the claims contribution 3
   rests on. Six options with costs, commitments, and anonymity interactions are in
   the checklist §3. **The sentence is untouched.**
   Related: `scripts/redact_check.py`'s allowlist labels `uda-lab/KSE2026` "public
   and citable", which is false today — a KSE2026 URL would pass `make redact`
   while being unreachable.
2. **`AGENTS.md` rule 6 disclosure scope.** Does ChatGPT-drafted *decision wording*
   fall inside 「原稿・分析への AI の関与」? The repo currently states three
   non-identical scopes (`AGENTS.md:23`, `provenance/ai-use.md:3` 「成果物」,
   `PLAN.md:211`) that a ruling should settle together. Three options with
   consequences are in the model §4.3. Option C (channel convention in the
   authority ledger rather than the AI-use log) is the only one requiring no
   unrecoverable reconstruction — stated as a fact, not a recommendation.
3. **Proposed rows for `provenance/author-decisions.md`** — *proposed here, not
   written*, per that file's 「確定判断のみ」 contract:
   - 2026-07-25 — decisions issued from the `t-uda` account are owner authority
     regardless of whether ChatGPT drafted the wording (Wave A flagged this as
     pending; the whole of #60 rests on it).
   - 2026-07-22 (or later) — submission anonymity is 保留, a decided deferral.
     Basis is a chat directive relayed through the orchestrator, so it needs owner
     confirmation before it becomes a row.
4. **A review has been awaiting human confirmation since 2026-07-20.**
   `provenance/review-history.md:8` records PR #1's internal scaffold review as
   「Claude Opus（サブエージェント）＋人間確認待ち」. All eight findings were fixed
   in that PR, so the pending item is the *confirmation*, not the work. Closing it
   is an owner act; surfaced here rather than dispositioned in the ledger.
5. **Candidate claims — proposed, not registered.** Registering or freezing is an
   owner act, and no new claim-bearing manuscript prose enters `paper/`; the only `paper/` change is the metadata switch in `paper/main.tex`, so no new claim is required.
   Three candidates, with the identifiers they would carry:
   - supervisory interventions reached the harness through more than one channel,
     with channel recorded separately from authority — `leray-hopf#1`, `#145`,
     `#146`, `#158`, EV-1669, EV-0247, `evidence/metrics/mediation-census.json`
   - in two recorded incidents the owner supplied the input that ended a fault
     state, once as an independent detection and once as a routine trigger, and
     the corpus distinguishes them — EV-1669, EV-0247, INC-005 (**blocked on the
     INC-005 amendment above**)
   - connector-mediated preparation produced both a correct release-blocking
     mathematical finding and an incomplete correction merged without independent
     review — `leray-hopf#158`, `#162`, `#170`, `#177`, `#178`, INC-001
6. **Byline for the non-anonymous branch** — `% TODO(owner)` in `main.tex`. Note
   that an affiliation email will fail `make redact`, which scans `paper/`.

## Wave C scope, as it now stands

Smaller than expected, because PR #59 already resolved items 1 and 2.

- **Required:** amend `INC-005`'s timeline with the owner's 06:30:55Z observation and explicit decision not to act; it must not be described as human detection.
- **Optional:** tighten `workflow-evolution.md:31`'s evidence cell with the two

Both branches were built and the file restored to `\anonymoustrue`.

body:
Follow-up to #61 (PR #63, merged as `b797810`). Two independent read-only reviewer subagents reviewed the merged change with different lenses and found defects that were not caught before merge. Full findings and disposition: https://github.com/uda-lab/KSE2026/pull/63#issuecomment-5073573111

None of these is a regression against the pre-#61 state, and no hard gate was weakened by #61 — that was independently verified. But three of them are latent deadlocks or inoperative protections that should not be left in place.

## Scope

**1. The ChkTeX install guard does not work (medium).**
`.github/workflows/checks.yml` asserts that `chktex --version | head -1` fails the job if the install did not take effect. It does not. GitHub's default step shell is `bash -e {0}`, without `pipefail`, so the pipeline's exit status is `head`'s and is always 0. Reproduced:

```
$ bash -e            -c 'chktex_missing --version | head -1'; echo $?   # 0
$ bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail -c 'chktex_missing --version | head -1'; echo $?   # 127
```

If `chktex` is ever absent while `apt-get` still exits 0, `make lint` takes its `chktex not installed; skipping` branch and CI reports green with half of the #59 lint gate silently retired. The same pattern applies to `latexmk --version | head -1` in `paper.yml`.

Fix: `shell: bash` on the install steps, plus a `REQUIRE_CHKTEX` mode so the `Makefile` cannot silently degrade regardless of shell semantics.

**2. `paper` is a selectable status-check context that will never report again (medium).**
The deleted `build.yml`'s *job* was named `paper`; the new *workflow* is named `paper`. GitHub's required-checks picker offers recently-reported contexts, so `paper` is offered as a legitimate choice. The real contexts are now `integrity` and `pdf`. An admin selecting `paper` — or `build` — deadlocks every PR permanently. This is the exact trap #61 set out to prevent, in a form the documentation does not warn about.

Fix: document `paper` and `build` as dead contexts that must never be required.

**3. Neither workflow triggers on `merge_group` (medium).**
"Require merge queue" sits beside "Require status checks to pass" in the Rulesets UI. Enabling both means `integrity` never reports for the `refs/gh-readonly-queue/...` ref, entries sit until the queue timeout and are dequeued, and nothing can merge.

Fix: add `merge_group:` to `checks.yml`.

**4. Lower-severity items.**
- `workflow_dispatch` and `push` to `main` share a concurrency group, so a merge can cancel an operator's manual full build — against #61 requirement 5.
- `paper.yml`'s header comment, `.github/workflows/README.md`, the root `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` all imply that any push to `main` runs `paper`. The YAML ANDs `branches` with `paths`. Behaviour is correct; the documentation is not.
- `cancel-in-progress` also applies to `main`; only the PR case is documented.
- Tag pushes trigger nothing, while the docs name releases as the archival path, implying a mechanism that does not exist.
- `checks.yml` says "roughly ten seconds"; the README says ~22 s; the measured run was 17 s.
- `AGENTS.md` says `make integrity` runs the same content as the `checks` workflow, which also runs `make lint`.
- Uppercase `.JSONL`/`.NDJSON` are matched by neither the old inline leakage guard nor the new script. Pre-existing; cheap to close.

## Acceptance criteria

- The ChkTeX gate cannot pass while ChkTeX did not run, verified by a test that removes the binary.
- `checks` reports a status for a merge-queue ref.
- Documentation names every context that must never be required, not only the one that is safe to require.
- No documentation statement about trigger behaviour contradicts the YAML.
- All four hard gates from #61 still block merges, unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Do not add a release or tag workflow; that is a separate archival decision.
- Do not enable branch protection. That remains the owner's call.
- Do not weaken claim verification, redaction, leakage protection or PDF validation.

body:
Sub-issue of #60 (Wave B). Wave A (#64, merged as `fe8fbeb`) delivered the evidence
layer: `performed_via_github_app` in the snapshot exporter, `analysis/mediation-census-methodology.md`,
and `evidence/metrics/mediation-census.{json,csv}`. Wave B builds the analysis layer on top of it.

## Scope

Three strands, one PR.

**B1 — role and authority model** (new `analysis/author-interface-model.md`)
Model the actors (human author, ChatGPT decision-support, GitHub Connector, Claude/Fable
orchestrators, implementing agents, reviewers) and separate **final authority** — the owner's,
undivided — from the separable functions of investigation, synthesis, recommendation, drafting,
and transmission. Carry a passage-by-passage audit ledger over every role/authority passage in
`paper/`, `claims/`, `analysis/`, `provenance/`, `notes/`, `AGENTS.md`, `PLAN.md`, `README.md`:
`file:line`, quote, disposition, reason.

Governing premise (issued by the owner 2026-07-25, not open for relitigation in this issue):
decisions issued from the `t-uda` account are owner-authority regardless of whether ChatGPT
drafted the wording. 「最終判断は常に scientific owner が行う」 and 「AI は著者にしない」 both
remain true. **The default disposition is therefore NO CHANGE**, and rewriting `scientific owner`
is out of scope.

Three narrower items are open, and they are claim-strength / disclosure questions rather than
authority questions:
1. `03-agent-workflow.tex` "until the supervisor caught the discrepancy" and `04-incidents.tex`
   "an incidental owner status check" — offered as evidence about *human detection*.
2. the word "direct" in `05-discussion.tex` ("the scientific owner's direct supervision"), which
   sits in a limitation sentence readers use to calibrate reproducibility.
3. `AGENTS.md` rule 6 disclosure scope — whether ChatGPT-drafted decision wording falls inside
   「原稿・分析への AI の関与」. Present options; the owner settles it.

**B2 — intervention traces** (new `analysis/author-interface-traces.md`)
Representative traces from the connector-attributed interventions, using Wave A's data and
cross-referencing `evidence/session-index/`, `evidence/incidents/INC-001..005`, and
`analysis/workflow-evolution.md`. Must include both effective mediation **and** drift (mistaken
summaries, weak recommendations, misread intent); a trace set containing only successes is
cherry-picking under PLAN.md §9 Phase 5. If no drift case is findable in the evidence, say so
explicitly and state what was searched. No productivity, effectiveness, or causal inference.
Every reconstruction carries `evidence_type` + confidence (AGENTS.md rule 5), and every trace is
anchored to a `make verify`-resolvable identifier.

**B3 — publication metadata**
- A LaTeX anonymity switch in `paper/main.tex` gating the byline and a `\thanks` funding
  acknowledgment ("This work was supported by JST-Mirai Program Grant Number JPMJMI22G1, Japan.",
  decided 2026-07-22, not yet present anywhere in `paper/`). Anonymity itself is 保留 — a decided
  deferral — so the switch ships defaulting to the current non-anonymous output.
- New `notes/deanonymization-checklist.md` enumerating every identity leak: the `uda-lab` URL in
  the `lerayhopf2026repo` bib entry, the leray-hopf PR numbers cited in Sections IV–V, and the
  acknowledgment.
- The artifact-availability gap: `05-discussion.tex` tells readers that evidence excerpts,
  manifests, and scripts are available "in the paper repository", but `uda-lab/KSE2026` is private
  and has no bib entry, URL, or DOI, so the sentence is unresolvable for a reader. Present options
  (make public / mint an archival DOI / soften the sentence) as an owner decision; do not decide it.

## Out of scope

- Writing `provenance/author-decisions.md` — that file records only the owner's confirmed decisions,
  each citing a re-derivable GitHub artifact. Proposed rows go in the PR body.
- Freezing any claim. New claims register as `Status: candidate`.
- Applying dispositions to `paper/` prose — that is Wave C, conditional on the B1 ledger.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `analysis/author-interface-model.md` exists, models the actors, and carries a complete
      passage-by-passage ledger re-derived from current `main` (not inherited from an earlier survey).
- [ ] `analysis/author-interface-traces.md` exists, covers both effective mediation and drift (or
      states explicitly and with search scope that drift cases were not findable), labels every
      reconstruction, and asserts no causal or productivity effect.
- [ ] `paper/main.tex` carries an anonymity switch gating byline + `\thanks` acknowledgment,
      defaulting to the current non-anonymous output; `make pdf` passes.
- [ ] `notes/deanonymization-checklist.md` enumerates every identity leak.
- [ ] Owner-decision items are collected in the PR body, not written into
      `provenance/author-decisions.md`.
- [ ] Gates: `make verify`; `scripts/redact_check.py` over evidence/claims/analysis/provenance/notes/paper;
      `git ls-files` shows no `^private/` beyond README.md and no `.jsonl`/`.ndjson`; `make lint`; `make pdf`.
- [ ] One row appended to `provenance/ai-use.md` (AGENTS.md rule 6).
- [ ] Independent review by reviewers other than the implementer, recorded on the PR.

Closes #62 (Wave A of parent #60; Wave B — role/authority model, intervention
traces, manuscript audit, anonymity decision — remains open on #60).

## What

Evidence-layer work only. No `paper/` changes, no `scientific owner` wording
changes.

1. Extended `scripts/export_repo_snapshot.py`'s issues and comments
   projections with `performed_via_github_app` (App slug or null) and
   `author_association`. Also added a `private` flag to `EXPORT.json`
   (fetched via `gh api repos/<repo>`) so snapshot consumers can see at a
   glance whether the export is publicly re-derivable.
2. Re-exported `evidence/repository-snapshots/leray-hopf/` at a fresh pinned
   `head_sha_at_fetch`/`fetched_at` — only `issues.json`, `comments.json`,
   `EXPORT.json` changed (commits/releases/tags identical, as expected).
3. Added a self-snapshot `evidence/repository-snapshots/KSE2026/`. Its
   `EXPORT.json` records `"private": true` and an explicit
   "REPRODUCIBILITY ASYMMETRY" note: unlike leray-hopf, this snapshot is
   reproducible only by an account with read access to the (private)
   KSE2026 repo.
4. Added `scripts/compute_mediation_census.py`, which groups both snapshots'
   issue/PR-creation and comment rows by `(login, performed_via_github_app)`
   and writes `evidence/metrics/mediation-census.{json,csv}`. Every emitted
   number carries a `lower_bound_caveat` field and is documented in the new
   `analysis/mediation-census-methodology.md`, following the house pattern of
   `analysis/usage-metrics-methodology.md`.
5. Updated `provenance/source-inventory.md` (new snapshot + derived-artifact
   rows) and appended one row to `provenance/ai-use.md`.

## Why "lower bound", not "census"

`performed_via_github_app: null` does not prove direct human authorship —
any PAT-holding process (gh CLI, orchestrator, harness) also yields null.
Demonstrated concretely on this repo's own PR #59: agent-generated `t-uda`
comments ("Final proposal gate for head…", "@codex please review this PR")

Closes #61

Splits the single `build` workflow into an always-running TeX-free gate
(`checks`) and a path-filtered PDF build (`paper`), both keyed by concurrency
so superseded runs are cancelled. Every measurement below was taken on this PR
or on a scratch PR opened against this branch.

## What changed

| file | role |
| --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/checks.yml` | new; always runs, no TeX; the workflow intended to be a required check |
| `.github/workflows/paper.yml` | new; path-filtered, TeX Live + PDF; must not be a required check |
| `.github/workflows/build.yml` | deleted (superseded) |
| `.github/workflows/README.md` | new; the two documentation acceptance criteria |
| `Makefile` | `make integrity` = verify + leakcheck + redact |
| `scripts/check_no_raw_logs.sh` | leakage guard extracted from inline YAML |
| `AGENTS.md` | documents `make integrity` and the two-workflow policy |

## Hard gates: unchanged in substance, only in placement

| gate | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scripts/verify_claim_links.py` | `build` | `checks` (always) and `paper` |
| redaction scan over 6 public dirs | `build` | `checks` (always) and `paper` |
| raw-log leakage guard | `build` | `checks` (always) and `paper` |
| `make lint` (unittest + prose scanner + ChkTeX) | `build` | `checks` (always) and `paper` |
| `make pdf` | `build` | `paper` (manuscript changes, `main`, dispatch) |

ChkTeX stays in the TeX-free workflow because the Debian `chktex` package is a
standalone 240 kB binary depending only on `libc6`, `libpcre2-posix3` and
`libtinfo6`; it does not pull in TeX Live. So the `make lint` gate added in #59
still runs on *every* PR rather than only manuscript ones. The install step
calls `chktex --version`, so a silently failed install fails the job instead of
letting `make lint` take its `chktex not installed; skipping` branch and pass a
weaker gate.

The three TeX-free gates now have one definition, `make integrity`, shared by
both workflows and by local runs.

## How the permanently-pending required-check trap is avoided

`checks` has **no path filter**, so it reports a status on every PR and is safe
to require. `paper` **is** path-filtered and must not be required: GitHub
reports *nothing at all* for a path-filtered workflow whose filter does not
match, so a required `paper` would sit pending forever on any PR that does not
touch the manuscript.

This is not just reasoned, it is demonstrated. Scratch PR #65 (closed) carried
a scripts-only diff against this branch. `gh pr checks 65` reported exactly one
status — `integrity` from `checks`, pass, 21s — and no `paper` status existed
that a branch-protection rule could ever have satisfied.

The accepted trade-off: `paper` cannot be enforced by branch protection. A
manuscript PR still cannot merge without a green PDF, because the merge gate
used here requires every *reported* check to have succeeded, and `paper` does
report on exactly those PRs. The repo currently has no branch protection
configured at all; `.github/workflows/README.md` states the intended policy for
when it is added.

## Case verification (observed, not predicted)

| case | expected | observed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| push to a PR branch | one run, not two | branch push produced **zero** `push` runs; only `pull_request` runs |
| PR touching only `scripts/` | `checks` only, merge not blocked | PR #65: only `integrity` ran (21s); no `paper` status |
| PR touching manuscript inputs | both run, PDF produced | this PR touches `Makefile`; `paper` ran and uploaded `paper-pdf` (240 KB) |
| two rapid pushes to one PR | first run cancelled | run 30117462984 cancelled 53s into the TeX install; lint/verify/redaction/PDF/upload all skipped |
| artifact retention | ~7 days | artifact created 2026-07-24, expires 2026-07-31 |

Note: `pull_request` path filters evaluate the PR's *cumulative* diff against
base, not the newest commit. A PR touching `paper/**` in any commit therefore
rebuilds the PDF on every later push — intended, since the artifact must match
the state that would merge.

## Measurements

Trigger/lifecycle, from this repository's run history and the runs on this PR:

| job | wall time | of which TeX provisioning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| old combined `build` | 95-105 s | 80-90 s |
| new `checks` | 22 s | none (ChkTeX install 12 s) |
| new `paper` | ~100 s | 70-90 s |

Over the 165 runs before this change: 96 `push` against 69 `pull_request` — the
duplication the issue describes.

TeX provisioning, run as sibling jobs on identical cold `ubuntu-latest` runners
in a single workflow run (30117463405) so the timings are directly comparable:

| route | provisioning | compile | total job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apt-get --no-install-recommends` (current) | 70 s | 2 s | **74 s** |
| `xu-cheng/latex-action@v4` | 92 s (provision + compile) | — | 94 s |
| `docker pull texlive/texlive:latest` | 107 s | 3 s | 112 s |

The current installation is the fastest of the three. Runners are ephemeral and
have no warm image cache, so a generic image pays its full pull cost every run:
`texlive/texlive:latest` is 5.53 GB against 393 MB of TeX actually installed by
the apt subset (381 MB `/usr/share/texlive` + 12 MB `/usr/share/texmf`). **No
image is adopted.**

**Not measured:** a small repository-specific GHCR image rebuilt on Dockerfile
change. It is the one route that could plausibly beat 70 s, and I am not
claiming otherwise. It would require publishing a package and a
rebuild-on-change workflow, which the issue lists as optional and not required
to close. The saving it competes for is now bounded by ~70 s on the minority of
PRs that touch the manuscript, against the standing cost of maintaining a
Dockerfile, a registry package and a rebuild workflow. Recorded as such in
`.github/workflows/README.md` rather than asserted either way.

The benchmark scaffold that produced these numbers
(`tex-provisioning-benchmark.yml`) was removed in cf5e74d.

## Local validation

- `make integrity` — claim links OK (2145 EV, 5 INC, 10 claims frozen); leakage guard clean; redaction 57 files / 0 findings
- `make lint` — 6 unit tests OK, prose scanner OK (7 TeX files), ChkTeX clean
- `actionlint` 1.7.7 on all workflows — clean (it also shellchecks `run:` blocks)
- `shellcheck` on `scripts/check_no_raw_logs.sh` — clean
- PyYAML parse of every workflow, asserting trigger/concurrency/job structure
- Fixture test of the leakage guard, 5 cases: clean tree (0), run from a subdirectory (0), tracked `private/` payload (1), tracked `.jsonl` (1), outside a git tree (2)
- `make pdf` could **not** be run locally — this container has no `latexmk` or `tectonic`. It is covered by the `paper` run on this PR, which built `build/main.pdf` (240 KB) in the same environment CI uses.

## Local Codex pre-review

Three findings; two fixed, one answered.

**Fixed — leakage guard failed open (medium).** With `pipefail` set but the
command substitution's exit status never consulted, an unreadable git index
produced an empty list and a clean exit 0. The inline YAML this replaced had the
same hole. Enumeration now goes through a temp file whose git status is checked
separately, and `git ls-files -z` with a NUL-delimited read loop replaces
line-oriented grep, since C-quoting hid names like `"weird.jsonl"`. Fixture
coverage went from 5 cases to 9, adding: newline in filename, space in filename,
corrupt index (now exit 2, previously a false clean), all verified.

**Fixed — the documented required check was wrong (high, doc half).** The README
said to require `checks`. GitHub reports the **job** name as the status context,
which is `integrity` — as observed on PR #65. Requiring `checks` would have
configured a context that never reports, causing exactly the permanent-pending
failure this split exists to avoid.

**Answered, not changed — the PDF build is not enforceable by branch protection
(high).** This is correct, and it is the trade-off issue #61 directs: an
always-running lightweight required workflow plus a separate conditional PDF
workflow. I have made the claim precise rather than restructure an
owner-approved design. What blocks a failed PDF today is the `github-driven-workflow`
merge gate, which requires every *reported* check to have succeeded — a
procedural gate, not a server-side one. `.github/workflows/README.md` now says
so explicitly, along with the fact that **no branch protection exists on this
repo at all**, before or after this change.

Two items for the owner, both out of scope here:

1. Branch protection is unconfigured. If added, require the context `integrity`.
2. Fully closing the PDF gap would need an always-reported job that inspects the
   cumulative PR diff and demands the PDF result only when manuscript inputs
   changed. Worth doing only alongside enabling protection.

## Non-goals respected

No custom CI image added. No weakening of claim verification, redaction,
leakage protection or final PDF validation — all four still gate merges, and
three of them now run on strictly *more* PRs than before, since `checks` has no
path filter while the old `build` workflow was equally unfiltered but far more
expensive.

## Problem

The current `build` workflow installs a substantial TeX Live subset and rebuilds the PDF on every `push`, every `pull_request` update, and every manual dispatch. On a PR branch, the same commit can therefore trigger both `push` and `pull_request` runs. Unrelated repository changes also pay the TeX installation and PDF-build cost.

The current cold build is not individually catastrophic, but repeating it for agent-generated incremental pushes is wasteful. GitHub-hosted runners are ephemeral, so replacing `apt-get` with a large generic TeX image does not by itself solve the problem: the image may still need to be pulled on every run.

## Owner-approved direction

Optimize **when** the expensive job runs before changing **how** TeX is provisioned.

### Required changes

1. **Eliminate duplicate PR-branch execution.**
   - Run `push` builds only on `main`.
   - Use `pull_request` for PR branch updates.
   - Keep `workflow_dispatch` for explicit full builds.

2. **Cancel superseded runs.**
   - Add workflow concurrency keyed by PR number or ref.
   - Set `cancel-in-progress: true` so a new agent push stops the obsolete build.

3. **Separate lightweight validation from the TeX/PDF job.**
   - Lightweight checks should remain available without installing TeX: claim-link verification, prose-scanner tests, raw-log leakage guard, redaction scan, and repository hygiene checks.
   - The TeX/PDF workflow should run only when relevant inputs change, including at least `paper/**`, bibliography/build inputs, `Makefile`, and the paper workflow itself.
   - Do not create a required-check configuration in which a path-filtered workflow remains permanently pending. Prefer an always-running lightweight required workflow and a separate conditional PDF workflow.

4. **Reduce artifact retention.**
   - PR PDF artifacts should be retained only briefly, approximately 7 days.
   - Durable publication artifacts belong in releases or another explicit archival path, not in every intermediate Actions run.

5. **Preserve explicit full validation.**
   - A paper-changing PR must still produce a PDF before merge.
   - `main` paper changes and manual dispatches must still run the complete lint, verification, leakage/redaction checks, and PDF build.

### TeX provisioning

Do not replace the current minimal Debian package installation with a generic full-TeX image without measurement.

After trigger and lifecycle fixes are implemented, compare cold-run timings for:

- the current `apt-get --no-install-recommends` installation;
- a maintained TeX GitHub Action or container with the required packages;
- optionally, a small repository-specific GHCR image rebuilt only when its Dockerfile changes.

Adopt an image only if it gives a clear cold-start or maintenance benefit. A custom image is not required for closing this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- A push to an open PR branch causes one relevant workflow execution, not duplicate `push` and `pull_request` builds.
- A new commit cancels an obsolete in-progress run for the same PR/ref.
- Changes unrelated to the manuscript do not install TeX or build the PDF.
- Lightweight integrity checks continue to run under the intended branch-protection policy.
- A manuscript-changing PR produces a validated PDF artifact.
- `main` and manual full builds remain supported.
- PR PDF artifacts use short retention.
- The workflow documentation states why execution frequency is constrained and why a generic TeX image was not adopted without measurement.

## Non-goals

- Do not add a large custom CI image merely for architectural neatness.
- Do not weaken claim verification, redaction, leakage protection, or final PDF validation.
- Do not perform full publication compression or figure work in this issue.

# Harness architecture figure specification

Tracked by issue #58. The scientific owner will draw and approve the final artwork.
The paper must remain readable until that artwork is added.

## Message

The figure presents a synthesized end-state architecture reconstructed from
controls introduced at different stages, not a configuration that existed
throughout the campaign. It separates scientific authority, implementation,
semantic adjudication, mechanical verification, runtime governance, and
evidence capture.

## Layout

Use a two-column IEEE `figure*`.

Central lifecycle:

1. Scientific owner
2. Issue and statement contract
3. Orchestrator
4. Issue-scoped implementing worktree
5. Pull request candidate
6. Applicable assurance gates
7. Merged project state
8. Release candidate
9. Full-build attestation
10. Attested release artifact

The assurance gateway is labeled `select gates by changed artifact` and
contains four distinct controls:

- semantic statement review and counterexample search;
- Lean build, axiom pin, and release-surface check;
- public-declaration comparison;
- review-completion record.

A read-only scout and a statement contract are conditional controls, used when
repository assumptions or mathematical scope require them. Semantic findings
return to the scientific owner and statement contract. Implementation and
mechanical findings return to the issue worktree. PR assurance advances a
candidate into the merged project state; release-candidate attestation is a
separate full-build boundary.

Two horizontal rails span the lifecycle:

- operational substrate: exclusive worktree ownership, liveness checks, shared
  build cache, global build lock, process cleanup, and available-memory monitoring;
- evidence rail: session, issue, PR, review, build, and release artifacts flow to
  the escrow/manifest and then to paper claims.

## Drawing constraints

- Use generic reader-facing terms, not model names, session IDs, EV codes, issue
  numbers, or Lean declaration names.
- Label arrows with short actions: `scope`, `bounded contract`, `committed diff`,
  `review finding`, `attested pass`, and `append evidence`.
- Distinguish semantic feedback to the owner/contract from technical feedback
  to the worktree.
- Mark the scout, statement contract, and declaration comparison as conditional
  rather than universal stages.
- Keep labels legible at two-column width and in grayscale.
- Supply vector PDF or SVG source and accessible alternative text.

## Caption draft

> Synthesized end-state architecture reconstructed from controls introduced at
> different stages of the Leray--Hopf campaign. Scientific authority,
> implementation, semantic adjudication, mechanical verification, runtime
> governance, and evidence capture follow separate paths; applicable checks are
> selected by the changed artifact, and release attestation occurs after pull-
> request assurance.

EV-2076, EV-0925, EV-1669, EV-0247, INC-001, INC-003, INC-004, and INC-005.

- Rewrite the abstract, introduction, formalization exposition, and conclusion so each has a distinct rhetorical function and does not repeat technical lists at the same level of detail.
- Minimize repository identifiers in reader-visible prose; introduce concepts before any retained Lean declaration or internal event name.
- Update claims, contribution mapping, repository guidance, planning documents, and provenance to match the revised hierarchy.

## Acceptance criteria

- The abstract, introduction, body, discussion, and conclusion do not repeat the same technical explanation or guardrail list at the same granularity.
- A reader who does not open the leray-hopf repository can explain: what was formalized; how the harness divided authority and verification; where each incident begins and ends; what response followed; and what qualified lesson transfers.
- The contribution hierarchy remains at most three items and maps each item to a result or method, prior baseline, concrete gain, evidence, and independent significance.
- New harness synthesis is registered as a claim before it appears in the manuscript, with observed evidence separated from causal or universal claims.
- Incident prose follows the common invariant → event → detection → response → lesson → evidence-strength structure.
- Reader-visible role names and harness terms are stable; model-specific routing, dispatch counts, event codes, issue numbers, and Lean identifiers appear only when they materially support the argument.

- `make verify`, public-content redaction scan, effective prose/LaTeX lint, and `make pdf` pass. Undefined references/citations and overfull boxes are absent.

body:
## 背景

repo 全体レビュー（2026-07-23）で，Phase 2 の証跡収集・incident 分析・billing 突合は十分に強い一方，Phase 3 の claim freeze と執筆前に再点検すべき横断事項が見つかった．本 issue は，既に進行中の執筆を止めず，改稿・adversarial review で回収する follow-up ledger とする．

構成性・計算可能性・古典論理依存の分析は重要な貢献候補だが，現時点では blocking としない．Lean 形式化の価値として一定程度自明でもあり，6ページの紙幅を見ながら改稿時に優先的に追加する optional 項目とする（関連する詳細作業は `uda-lab/leray-hopf-notes#115` に既にある）．

## P0/P1 follow-up

### 1. Related work baseline を確定する（TauCeti を含む）

`notes/related-work.md` と `claims/contribution-map.md` の baseline が未確定のまま contribution 文言が先行している．少なくとも次を一次資料に基づいて埋める．

- **TauCeti** を明示的な比較対象に追加する．まず正式な paper / repo / version を特定し，書誌情報を固定する．
- 比較軸は，単発 theorem proving / benchmark 成績ではなく，project-scale formalization，human steering，multi-agent role separation，proof assistant feedback，artifact governance，session/evidence preservation，incident recovery，resource/cost reporting とする．
- TauCeti との実質的差分は一次資料を読んだ後にのみ書き，名称だけから推測しない．
- 解析学・PDE の既存形式化，大規模 Lean プロジェクト，agentic theorem proving / software-engineering case study も最低限の baseline 行を作る．

### 2. CLM-004 / CLM-005 の主張強度を校正する

#### CLM-004

符号化 6 セッションは purposive sample であり，全キャンペーンの悉皆標本でも無作為標本でもない．したがって，

- `FALSE-SUCCESS = 0` は「符号化済み6セッション内で観測されなかった」という記述統計に限定する．
- 「commit 前 disk 再検証や adversarial review の**帰結**」という因果解釈は外すか，`consistent with` 程度に弱める．
- prevalence，failure rate，guardrail effectiveness の推定には使わない．

#### CLM-005

INC-001 / INC-002 は有益な対照例だが，現行の「帰結を分けたのは独立 statement 検査の有無だった」は因果表現が強い．

- `The paired cases provide a contrast consistent with the value of independent statement review.` 程度へ弱める．
- 観測事実（INC-001 では独立検査が行われず残存，INC-002 では独立検査時に検出）と，反実仮想（検査さえあれば必ず防げた）を分ける．

### 3. Vertex Cloud Monitoring `token_count` と cache token の対応を検証する

Google Cloud の公式 metric 記述では `publisher/online_serving/token_count` は accumulated **input/output token count** で，`type=input/output` と `explicit_caching` label を持つ．一方，現行 `scripts/extract_vertex_phase.py` は escrow 側の model total として

```text
input + output + cache_read + cache_write
```

を合算し，Monitoring total との差を「物理的上限」として FX 下界同定に使っている．公式記述だけから，Monitoring の input token が Anthropic usage / billing SKU の cache-read・cache-write token をどのように含むかは自明でない．

確認事項:

- raw Monitoring export に `type=input/output` と `explicit_caching` の内訳が残っているか．
- Vertex の Claude endpoint において monitoring input count が `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens` に対応するのか，別定義か．
- billing SKU の input/cache-read/cache-write と metric の input/output を同一母数へ写す根拠を一次資料または実測セルで示せるか．

解決できない場合:

- FX 下界 `[160.4, ...]` と leray 単独費用区間を「当該 metric interpretation の下での導出」と明示する，または下界推定を外す．
- `billing reconciliation is completely closed` という表現を避ける．
- machine-wide provider-billed actual cost `¥54,867.9` と，escrow usage の API-equivalent `$258.28` は独立に維持できる．

公式 metric reference: https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/metrics_gcp_a_b （`publisher/online_serving/token_count`）

### 4. CLM-002 の campaign scope から KSE 論文作業を分離する

現行 CLM-002 は `2026-06-10〜07-21` の「形式化キャンペーン」としているが，usage JSON には 07-21 local-secondary の KSE2026 証跡収集・論文作業セッションが含まれる．

推奨:

- 形式化キャンペーンの終端を release `2026-07-20` に固定し，再集計する．
- script に campaign end / session allowlist を明示的に持たせ，後日の paper 作業ログが再実行時に混入しないようにする．
- 別案として範囲を `leray-hopf-related development and evidence-preservation activity` に改称できるが，論文上は形式化本体と paper 作業を分離する方が明快．

### 5. repo hygiene / verification の follow-up

- README の Phase 1/2 進捗表示を現状へ同期する．
- README / AGENTS の `tectonic 優先` 表記を，Makefile と owner decision の `latexmk/pdflatex 優先，tectonic fallback` に同期する．
- `provenance/source-inventory.md` の GitHub issue/PR snapshot「未収集」を更新する．
- `verify_claim_links.py` が実際には検査していない `leray-hopf@sha` / `leray-hopf#num` / `decl:<name>`，frozen-only policy について，実装を強化するか文書上の保証を弱める．
- `extract_metrics.py` の first commit date 取得を root commit 明示方式へ直す．textual `sorry` count と release import cone の sorry-free claim を混同しない．
- incident card の `FALSE-SUCCESS` 分類と集計定義を同期する．
- Unix の zombie state でない残留プロセスを paper では `stale/orphaned side-process chain` 等と呼び，「ゾンビ」を技術用語として誤用しない．

## Optional: 構成性・計算可能性

紙幅と改稿バランスを見て，Contribution 1 または Discussion に短く加える候補:

- finite-dimensional Galerkin data / ODE layer
- `Nonempty` / `Exists` による包装
- compactness・subsequence・limit selection
- explicit witness を与えた後の assembly / limit-passage 再利用
- `Classical.choice`，`noncomputable`，proof-only classical dependency の区別

本 issue では全依存 cone の監査を要求しない．余白があれば優先的に取り込む．

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TauCeti の正式な一次資料が特定され，related-work baseline と比較軸が記録される
- [ ] CLM-004 が符号化6セッション内の記述統計に限定される
- [ ] CLM-005 の因果表現が観測的な対照へ弱められる
- [ ] Monitoring token と cache SKU の対応が根拠付きで解決されるか，FX/費用 claim が条件付きへ弱められる
- [ ] CLM-002 が 07-21 paper/evidence activity を形式化 campaign から分離する
- [ ] README / inventory / build-engine 記述が現状と同期する
- [ ] claim verification と formalization metrics の保証範囲が実装・文書間で一致する

body:
## 背景

現行の `CLM-002` / `analysis/usage-metrics-methodology.md` は，収集済み Claude Code ログから token usage を再構成し，公表 API 単価による **API-equivalent cost** を算出している．これは全キャンペーンの規模を示す下界として有用だが，provider からの実請求額とは区別する必要がある．

一方，証明を最終的に完成させた 2026 年 7 月上旬の一部期間では，Fable 5 を Vertex AI 上で運用しており，Google Cloud 側の billing record から token usage・実請求額・対象期間を比較的精密に取得できる見込みである．この期間を，対応する issue / PR / commit / axiom frontier の変化と結び付ければ，大規模 agentic formalization の完成フェーズについて，監査可能な resource profile を提示できる．

これは単なる費用メモではなく，類似規模の自動・半自動形式化を計画する研究者にとって，必要な推論資源と実支出の実例となる．また，Vertex 費用の支出元となった研究費・支援への成果還元と，論文中の acknowledgment を正確に記述する基礎資料にもする．

## 方針

次の二つを明確に分離する．

1. **全キャンペーンの再構成推定値**
   - セッションログ上の usage と公表単価から算出した `API-equivalent cost`
   - 欠損ログを含むため下界
   - 実請求額とは呼ばない

2. **Vertex 完成フェーズの実測値**
   - Google Cloud billing record に基づく `provider-billed actual cost`
   - 対象期間，project / service / SKU，credit・discount，currency を明示
   - 同期間のセッション usage および形式化上の進捗と照合

比較実験ではないため，`cost-effectiveness` や「この金額で証明全体を完成できる」といった因果・一般化主張は行わない．位置付けは **audited resource profile of the final completion campaign** または **marginal cost of the final axiom-elimination phase** とする．

## 調査項目

- Vertex AI を使用した正確な開始・終了日時と関連セッションを特定する
- 当該期間に使用した model / endpoint / host / orchestrator 構成を記録する
- セッションログから token usage を対象期間だけ再集計する
- Google Cloud Billing から次を取得する
  - service / SKU
  - usage dates
  - gross cost
  - credits / discounts
  - net cost
  - currency
- Vertex AI 推論費と，該当する場合の Compute Engine / disk / network 費を分離する
- billing 側と session usage 側の時間帯・集計粒度・課金単位の差を説明する
- 同期間の leray-hopf の issue / PR / commit / axiom frontier の変化を対応付ける
- 支出元となった研究費・支援制度の正式名称，grant number，acknowledgment 文言を scientific owner が確認する

## 成果物案

```text
evidence/metrics/
├── campaign-usage-estimate.json
├── vertex-completion-phase-usage.json
├── vertex-completion-phase-billing.csv
└── vertex-completion-phase-summary.json

analysis/
├── billing-reconciliation.md
└── cost-attribution-methodology.md
```

生の請求明細，billing account ID，project ID，個人情報等は Git に載せない．公開領域には redaction 済み集計のみを置き，raw export は `private/` 側で保存・hash 登録する．

## Claim 整理

現行 `CLM-002` をそのまま実請求額の主張へ拡張せず，少なくとも次の二層に分ける．

- 全期間の token / active-session-hours / API-equivalent cost の再構成推定
- Vertex 完成フェーズの provider-billed actual cost と，対応する形式化成果

後者を独立 claim とするか，resource-profile table の根拠に留めるかは Phase 3 の contribution freeze で scientific owner が判断する．

## 論文での提示候補

小表一つで，次を対応付ける．

| Phase | Dates | Formalization outcome | Model/backend | Token usage | Actual billed cost |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| Final axiom-elimination / completion | TBD | issue・PR・axiom frontier で記述 | Fable 5 via Vertex AI | TBD | TBD |

Acknowledgment と resource analysis は分離する．本文では Vertex AI を計算環境として記述し，first-page footnote / acknowledgment では費用を支出した正式な助成機関・研究費を記載する．

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Vertex 使用期間と対象セッションが一次資料に基づき固定されている
- [ ] provider-billed actual cost と API-equivalent cost が明確に分離されている
- [ ] gross / credits / net / currency / service・SKU の扱いが文書化されている
- [ ] billing record と session usage の照合方法・不一致要因が記録されている
- [ ] 対象期間の形式化成果が issue / PR / commit / declaration に対応付けられている
- [ ] raw billing data が Git 管理下に入っていない
- [ ] 公開集計が `redact_check.py` / `make verify` を通る
- [ ] `claims/paper-claims.md` と `analysis/usage-metrics-methodology.md` が新しい区分に同期している
- [ ] 研究費 acknowledgment の正式文言候補が `notes/` または `provenance/author-decisions.md` に記録されている
